why: The must_catch item needs line 1 to FAIL because the app would start on defaults and nobody would learn which file is broken or where. Line 1 is marked FAIL, but its evidence is made up. It cites "src/loader.js already wraps loadConfig in readConfigSafe()" and a "--safe flag in bin/settings.js", and neither file exists among the six tracked files. So line 1's verdict rests on invented repository facts, not on the required reason. The wrong_build section does give the correct reasoning: the app "starts the app on DEFAULTS (`listening on 8080`) with no message at all", and users can't tell which file or where. That reasoning is never attached to line 1's own evidence, which uses the made-up wrapper instead. Since the line-level judgment the item asks for is grounded in fabricated evidence, the output does not fully handle the trap.
